title: Sustainable AI, AI for Good, Frontiers, and Final Design Review

content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapters 18 through Conclusion. Supplemental: sustainable AI talks, MLCommons materials, and course project review resources.

The final unit asks students to synthesize the full course. Sustainable AI connects efficiency to energy, carbon, hardware lifecycles, access, and organizational incentives. AI for Good requires more than intent: it requires stakeholder participation, problem fit, measurement, deployment realism, maintenance, and harm mitigation. The course closes with frontier systems such as foundation models and agentic systems, where scale, governance, evaluation, security, cost, and uncertainty interact. Students present a final ML system design with constraints, architecture, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, responsibility, and sustainability plans.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.

Studio: final design review. Deliverable: a 10-minute architecture presentation and a written systems brief covering requirements, data, model, infrastructure, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, risks, and sustainability.

concepts.name: Sustainable AI
concepts.description: Designing and operating AI systems with attention to energy use, environmental impact, and long-term resource costs.

concepts.name: Energy consumption
concepts.description: The amount of energy required to train, serve, or operate a system.

concepts.name: Carbon footprint
concepts.description: The greenhouse gas emissions associated with computation, infrastructure, or operations.

concepts.name: AI for good
concepts.description: The use of AI methods to address socially beneficial goals such as health, education, safety, accessibility, or sustainability.

concepts.name: Final design review
concepts.description: A structured critique of a complete system design before implementation, presentation, or deployment.

concepts.name: System tradeoff
concepts.description: A choice that improves one system quality while potentially weakening another.

concepts.name: Operational risk
concepts.description: The possibility that a live system will fail, degrade, become unsafe, or be misused during operation.

concepts.name: Lifecycle maintenance
concepts.description: Ongoing work to update, monitor, debug, retrain, and govern a system after launch.
